description: metresBetween(lat1,lng1,lat2,lng2) is the same haversine formula as private.metres_between() in schema.sql (12,742,000 m mean earth diameter) — the two must never quietly disagree about proximity. Because trig implementations can differ by fractions of a metre across platforms (JS vs. Swift vs. Kotlin), assert metresBetween results within toleranceMetres of expectedMetres, not by exact equality. formatDistance(metres) and sortByDistance(machines, from) are exact-equality checks — they're pure arithmetic/formatting/sort, not trig.

metresBetweenCases.description: A point and itself is zero metres apart.
Two points ~78 m apart on the same street — the everyday case, not the country-scale one.
Praça do Comércio (Lisbon) to Praça da Liberdade (Porto) — a real, checkable country-scale distance a Swift/Kotlin port can verify its haversine against.
Same two points, arguments swapped — the distance doesn't care which point is 'from'.

formatDistanceCases.description: 437 m, the exact case CLAUDE.md calls out — nobody needs 'a 437 m'.
The 'a 1,2 km' example from the brief.
997 m rounds to 1000 m at the nearest-10 step, which must push it into the km bucket rather than displaying 'a 1000 m'.
9951 m rounds to 10,0 km at the one-decimal step, which must push it into the whole-km bucket rather than displaying 'a 10,0 km'.
Country-scale distance (the Lisbon-Porto reference above): no decimal, nobody needs 275,25 km precision.

sortByDistanceCases.description: from is null: original order is preserved (the fix isn't known yet, so there's nothing to sort by).
Three points on the same meridian at clearly separated distances from 'from' — nearest sorts first regardless of input order.
